title: Data Type Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Drag Python value cards such as 3.0, "42" and (2026, 9, 28) into bins for int, float, str, bool, list and tuple, with hints for wrong answers.

learningObjectives: Classify a written Python value as int, float, str, bool, list or tuple
Name the clue that marks each type: a decimal point, quote marks, True/False, square brackets or parentheses
Explain why "42" is a string and 3.0 is a float even though both look like whole numbers
prerequisites: Typing values in the Thonny REPL
The type() function from this chapter

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Sorting game with immediate corrective feedback
keyQuestions: What single clue tells you a value is a string?
How do you tell a list from a tuple at a glance?
commonMisconceptions: A value made of digits is always a number, even inside quotes
Any whole-looking number such as 3.0 is an int
The words True and "True" mean the same thing
assessmentOpportunities: Students sort at least 14 of 16 cards correctly on the first try.
Students can explain why `"42"` is a `str` and `3.0` is a `float`.
Students can write one new example value for each of the six types.

controls.label: Shuffle and Restart
controls.description: Deals all 16 cards again in a new order and clears the score

controls.label: Value card
controls.description: Drag the top card onto a bin, or click a bin to drop it there
